data.title: Tesla Plans Six New Superchargers in Malaysia by Year-End
data.description:
Tesla is planning to expand its Supercharger network in Malaysia with six additional stations before the end of 2026, building on the company’s growing charging infrastructure across the country.

According to Tesla Malaysia, the company currently operates 21 Supercharger stations with a total of 92 charging stalls nationwide, up from 15 stations and 68 stalls a year ago.

The six new stations are expected to open in Kuala Lumpur, Selangor, Perak, Negeri Sembilan (Seremban), and Penang.

The expansion plans were highlighted during a presentation at Tesla’s Cybercab preview event in Malaysia on Thursday. (via PaulTan).

While Tesla had previously announced the six upcoming charging locations, the presentation provided another look at the company’s plans for the remainder of the year.

Tesla is also planning additional stations beyond these six locations, although those projects are still awaiting approval from local authorities.

Meanwhile, Tesla’s Destination Charging network in Malaysia has also grown over the past year, although at a slower pace than its Supercharger network.

The company currently operates 18 Destination Charging stations with 78 chargers, compared to 16 stations and 73 chargers at the same time last year.

Tesla also ended free access to its Destination Charging network in Malaysia earlier this year, with the company introducing paid charging in July.

data.title: SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell Gifts Over 2 Million Shares to U.S. Children
data.description:
SpaceX President and COO Gwynne Shotwell has announced a gift of more than 2 million SpaceX shares to American children, following Elon Musk’s own share giveaway announcement earlier this month.

According to Shotwell’s announcement on X, the shares are a personal gift from her and her husband Robert, with distribution through children’s Trump Accounts scheduled for December.

The program is limited to eligible children in the United States, meaning Canadian children will not qualify.

“Robert and I are thrilled that our gift of over 2 million shares of SpaceX stock will be distributed to children’s Trump accounts in December!” Shotwell wrote.

Shotwell shared the details in a post on X.

The initial distribution will cover children aged 11 to 17 living in ZIP codes where median family income is US$57,000 (C$79,800) or less.

Children in areas with populations too small for the census to report median family income will also qualify. Eligible families should receive notifications by Monday.

Shotwell said the shares are already being transferred into escrow ahead of the December distribution.

Meanwhile, a second gift is expected to be finalized in the coming weeks, expanding eligibility to children in military families serving overseas and those in foster care.

It will also include eligible children living in certain Texas counties where median family income is US$90,000 (C$126,000) or less.

The announcement follows Musk’s October 19 pledge to give one SpaceX share to every child in America next year, a proposed giveaway potentially worth US$10.5 billion (C$14.9 billion).

data.title: Musk Denies Reports that Optimus Orders Will Go Live in December
data.description:
Elon Musk has gone to X to deny reports that Tesla’s Optimus reservations will open in early December.

The original rumour comes from Modar Alaoui, an investor at ALM Ventures, who told The Standard that Optimus reservations will be timed around the upcoming Humanoids Summit on December 1-2. Tesla is a key partner for the conference and is planning to demo the Optimus V3 and launch reservations shortly thereafter.  

When asked on X whether consumers could order an Optimus in December, the Tesla CEO quickly said no.

The Optimus has piqued interest both for commercial and personal applications. However, it is unclear how many humanoid robots will be available for eventual consumer purchase, and Tesla has not released a price.

Tesla’s focus right now is commercial applications, including working in warehouses, factories and packing and sorting facilities. Once the commercial side is operating and shipping to companies, we may see Tesla start shipping a limited number of Optimus units to consumers.

During Tesla’s October earnings call, Musk noted that Optimus still has issues, including AI, runtime, and electromechanical design concerns. However, he confirmed the goal is to fix these by the end of next year for deliveries to companies outside of Tesla.

data.title: Tesla Owner Discovers Costly Consequence of Activating Emergency Drive Away Feature, Even With No Damage
data.description:
Tesla owners who activate the new Emergency Drive Away feature could face a US$539 (C$754) service charge, even if they never actually use the safety feature and drive away.

According to a post on X by Yaro (@Tutrifour), one of their customers called after accidentally activating the feature while the charge cable was still connected.

The owner had tapped Activate and was preparing to drive away before remembering the charging cable was still connected. Fortunately, they stopped before moving.

However, simply activating the feature triggered a warning that could only be cleared by Tesla Service, even though the vehicle never moved.

A screenshot from Service Mode showed the active alert “BMS_a228_EmergencyDriveAwayServiceRequired,” indicating the vehicle required service after the feature was activated.

In a follow-up post on Friday, Yaro revealed the cost to have the warning cleared.

“Don’t press Activate on the new Emergency Drive Away feature on your Tesla because service charges $539 to inspect the charge port and to clear the alert. Yes, even if you didn’t move the car an inch.”

Tesla introduced Emergency Drive Away with software update 2026.38.3, allowing drivers to disconnect from a Supercharger by driving away with the charging cable still attached during an emergency.

To activate it, drivers must attempt to shift into Drive while plugged in, hold the brake pedal, and tap Activate.

Tesla warns that using the feature will damage both the vehicle and Supercharger, with potential electrical and civil costs reaching US$25,000 (C$35,000).

Tesla also warned that using the feature would require vehicle repairs, but as it turns out, simply activating it can lead to a hefty service bill, even if the vehicle never moves and no damage occurs.

data.title: esla Pushes Australia to Fast-Track Autonomous Vehicle Laws by Two Years
data.description:
Tesla has called on the Australian government to allow autonomous vehicle trials on public roads in 2027, citing new safety data from its Full Self-Driving (FSD) system and delays in national regulations.

According to Tesla’s October 16 submission to the Senate Select Committee on Productivity in Australia, the company wants permits for public-road trials while a national regulatory framework is developed.

Tesla is also asking the government to accelerate the proposed Autonomous Vehicle Safety Law (AVSL), bringing its expected implementation forward from 2029 to 2027.

The company argues that faster adoption could improve road safety, pointing to the Federal Government’s own research, which estimated that autonomous vehicles could save up to 800 lives annually at full adoption.

Tesla also cited independent modelling from the Autonomous Vehicle Association of Australia, estimating that accelerating the legislation by two years could deliver more than A$10 billion (C$9.8 billion) in benefits.

Since launching FSD (Supervised) in September 2025, Tesla vehicles have travelled more than 160 million kilometres with the system activated across Australia and New Zealand.

Tesla reported 40% fewer collisions, 90% fewer harsh braking incidents and 86% fewer harsh acceleration events compared with its vehicles operating without FSD engaged.

data.title: Elon Musk says Neuralink’s Blindsight is ready, awaiting regulatory approval
data.description:
Elon Musk shared new details on Thursday night about Neuralink’s first two products, Telepathy and Blindsight, as the brain implant company continues running clinical trials, including its CAN-PRIME study in Canada.

According to Musk, Neuralink’s first product, Telepathy, allows users to communicate with computers or other people simply by thinking, with major improvements expected in the coming years.

“Output bandwidth will vastly exceed the fastest human speech or typing in a few years. Read that sentence again,” Musk said.

Musk also provided an update on Blindsight, Neuralink’s second product, which is being developed to restore vision to people who are blind, including those who have never seen before.

“It is ready from an engineering standpoint. Just waiting on regulatory approval,” Musk said.

Blindsight received Breakthrough Device Designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in September 2024, although that designation does not constitute approval for commercial use.

The updates came as Neuralink detailed a recent 72-hour hackathon, during which engineers worked with a speech restoration study participant to improve communication using its brain-computer interface (BCI).

Among the developments was automatic detection of when a user intends to speak, removing the need to manually start and stop recording speech intentions.

Engineers also improved Bloom, Neuralink’s mobile speech app, adding iPhone call integration that allows generated speech to be heard directly by the person receiving the call.

Another prototype allowed users to activate a Grok agent by simply thinking the phrase “Hey Neuralink,” followed by a task they wanted completed.

data.title: SpaceX Challenges T-Mobile’s Proposed Satellite Phone Rules
data.description:
As satellite-to-phone services start to fight traditional carriers for spectrum, SpaceX has gone to the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to complain about T-Mobile.

In a filing with the FCC, SpaceX complains that T-Mobile is pushing antiquated technical rules that should apply only to ground-based cell sites. The not-so-subtle section in the filing states:

SpaceX has worked extensively with other operators, including T-Mobile, through the WRC-27 Advisory Committee process to reach consensus. Unfortunately, the misplaced desire to harm a competitor has led many incumbents to oppose modernized rules that would bring direct-to-cell service to underserved border communities.

The filing concerns the upcoming 2027 World Radiocommunication Conference, an international forum where nations meet to update and revise existing radio regulations. Unsurprisingly, mobile satellite services for phones are on the agenda, as the conference is examining radio spectrum rules and allocations for these new entrants.

This latest spat between T-Mobile and SpaceX stems from T-Mobile’s proposal to prevent potential issues between satellite providers and terrestrial cell towers at border locations. To prevent interference, T-Mobile has proposed a 400 km radio interference protection zone around base stations near border cell towers.

The fight over spectrum, its rules, and allocations isn’t going away anytime soon as SpaceX continues to push into traditional terrestrial cell phone territory. Least to say, the FCC will be busy with filings, rulings, and proposals from both sides for the next few years.

data.title: Tesla Launches Heat Pump Optimization for Powerwall 3 Owners in Europe
data.description:
Tesla has introduced a new Heat Pump Optimization feature for Powerwall 3, allowing compatible heat pumps to use surplus solar energy or cheaper electricity to help homeowners reduce heating costs.

According to Tesla Energy, the feature is available for Powerwall 3 and Powerwall 3P in Europe, where it can automatically adjust heating based on solar production and electricity prices.

The system works by increasing heating when excess solar energy is available or electricity rates are low, storing that energy as heat for later use.

As explained in Tesla’s installation documentation, Heat Pump Optimization supports compatible Smart Grid Ready (SG-Ready) heat pumps that can receive control signals from an external energy management system.

There are two operating modes. In Normal mode, the heat pump follows its regular thermostat settings, while Boosted mode raises target temperatures to store additional energy in hot water or buffer tanks.

When Powerwall is set to Self-Powered mode, excess solar production activates Boosted mode. In Savings mode, the system can also activate it when electricity prices are low.

However, when solar production drops or electricity rates increase, the heat pump returns to Normal mode, reducing the need to consume more expensive electricity.

While Powerwall 3 has been available in Canada since May 2024, Tesla has not announced Heat Pump Optimization for Canadian customers or provided a timeline for a North American rollout.

data.title: Tesla Semi Wins Top Gear Tech Award
data.description:
Top Gear has awarded the Tesla Semi its Tech Award, praising the electric truck as a reminder of Tesla at its best.

Influential UK-based auto media house Top Gear has recognised the Tesla Semi with the Tech Award. In the 2027 edition of the US Car Awards, the electric truck is described as Tesla at its brilliant best. According to Top Gear:

“One thing is for sure: this is the version of Tesla we want to see. The version focused on making important vehicles that serve normal people brilliantly. Amid all the recent noise, it’s become all too easy to forget what this company is capable of at its brilliant best. The Semi is a potent reminder.”

Tesla refreshed the Semi in September with a light bar at the front, electric steering, a heat pump, and many more changes “under the hood.”

The automaker offers two versions: Standard and Long Range, with 325-mile and 500-mile driving ranges respectively when fully loaded. The Semi can even travel further its advertised range when carrying lighter loads.

It can also charge at 1.2 MW, allowing it to go from 0 to 60 percent in just 30 minutes with a Megacharger.

Tesla produces the Semi in Nevada, with a capacity of 50,000 trucks per year. Tesla will start shipping to Europe in 2027.

A pre-production Tesla Semi caught fire days ago, shutting down a California highway for hours. No cause has been given for the blaze.

data.title: F1 champion Nico Rosberg praises Tesla FSD as “life changing”
data.description:
For the second time in less than a week another Formula 1 World Champion has praised Tesla’s self-driving technology, with Nico Rosberg sharing his experience just days after Damon Hill took a driverless Cybercab ride in Austin.

According to a LinkedIn post shared Friday, Rosberg has been testing Tesla’s Full Self-Driving (FSD) (Supervised) in a Cybertruck while attending meetings around San Francisco.

The 2016 F1 World Champion and founder of Rosberg Ventures described the experience as life-changing, saying the technology has made his busy schedule easier to manage.

“I’ve been test-driving the Tesla Cybertruck with Full Self-Driving around San Francisco… and it’s been LIFE-CHANGING!,” he said. (via EVWire)

Rosberg explained that he had back-to-back meetings across the city, but using FSD made his commutes less tiring and helped him arrive feeling more focused. He even managed to spend some quality time with his wife during one of the drives.

“My whole racing career, I was the one in control behind the wheel. But I’m now fully willing to hand over control!!” Rosberg wrote.

His comments come shortly after fellow F1 champion Damon Hill, who won the championship in 1996, experienced Tesla’s Cybercab in Austin following the United States Grand Prix.

Unlike Rosberg’s supervised Cybertruck experience, Hill’s ride was driverless, with the former champion sharing a 79-second video of the experience.

Rosberg added that Europe is falling behind in assisted-driving technology and called for faster progress in bringing these systems to the region. Currently only 10 EU countries have approved FSD following the provisional approval in the Netherlands earlier this year. To appease regulators in the region, Tesla also renamed FSD Tesla Assisted Driving.
